### Multi-Omics to understand diseases {background-color="#534AB7"}

From a GWAS hit to a drug target — this is what this course builds toward:

```         
GWAS / PRS                            → Which genetic variants increase disease risk?
    🔽
Epigenomics                           → Which regulatory elements are involved?
    🔽
Metagenomics                          → Does the microbiome play a role?
    🔽
Transcriptomics (bulk RNA-seq)        → Which genes are involved?
    🔽
Transcriptomics (scRNA-seq/Spatial)   → Which cell types? In which tissue context?
    🔽
Proteomics                            → Which actual players are involved?
    🔽
Multi-omics                           → How do all these layers converge on a target?
    🔽
Disease prediction                    → Can we predict diseases?
Drug Discovery                        → Can we reposition an existing drug?
```

::: fragment
▶️ Every tool we learn is a **piece of the same puzzle**
:::

## 2. R Environment Setup

### Principles of a Reproducible Workflow

Three things that will save you later:

1.  **Project-based** working — never `setwd()` again
2.  **Consistent directory structure** — know where everything lives
3.  **Locked package versions** — your code runs the same in 2 years

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 1) R Project (.Rproj)

::: fragment
R env file to fix your working directory
:::

::: fragment
#### how to create R project

```         
RStudio → File → New Project → New Directory (or Existing Directory)
```

![](/assets/img/w1/R%20project.png){fig-align="center"}
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### recommended structure of folders

```         
my_project/
├── my_project.Rproj                 ← setting working directory where this file exists
├── scripts/                         ← R scripts (.R)
│   ├── 1_table1.R
│   ├── 2_preprocessing.R
│   └── 3_figure.R
├── rawdata/                         ← raw data (never change)
│   └── clinical_data.xlsx
├── analysis/                        ← preprocessed data
│   ├── 1_cleaned_data.rds
│   ├── 1_df_pt.rds
│   ├── 1_table1.rds
│   ├── 2_df_pt_processed.rds
│   ├── 3_cox_model.rds
│   ├── 3_cox_tidy.rds
└── results/                         ← final results
│   ├── Table1.docx
│   ├── KM_OS.tiff
│   └── forest_OS.tiff
└── logs/ or docs/                   ← whatever
```

### 2) renv: for reproducible environments

```{r}
# 1. Initialize — run once when starting a project
renv::init()

# 2. Install packages as usual
install.packages("Seurat")
BiocManager::install("DESeq2")

# 3. Snapshot — lock your current package versions
renv::snapshot()

# 4. Restore — on a new machine or for a collaborator
renv::restore()
```

::: callout-note
### Why this helps

Without `renv`, a Seurat update 6 months from now may silently break your code.
:::

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 3) Hands-On: Let's Set Up Together

① Create a new R Project

```         
File → New Project → New Directory → New Project
Name: "advanced_BI"
```

② Create directory structure

```{r}
dirs <- c("rawdata", "analysis", 
          "results/figures", "results/tables", 
          "scripts", "logs")
sapply(dirs, dir.create, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

③ Initialize renv

```{r}
install.packages("renv")
renv::init()
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

④ Install core packages for this semester

```{r}
# CRAN packages
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "BiocManager", 
                   "ggplot2", "patchwork", "data.table"))

# Bioconductor
BiocManager::install(c("DESeq2", 
                       "SingleR", "celldex"))

# Snapshot your environment
renv::snapshot()
```

::: callout-note
Some packages (Seurat, ArchR) we'll install in the relevant week.\
Bioconductor installs can take a few minutes — this is normal.
:::
